Independently ran the test file against this exact source: all 6 cases pass, and `tsc --noEmit` is clean project-wide. Cross-checked every dependency the module imports (`gh/op-table.ts`'s `field`/`fieldSchema`/`refuseInput`/`OpDef`/`FieldSpec`, `shell-helper.ts`'s `runShellBytes`, `types.ts`'s `ApprovalClass`/`ToolApprovalGate`/`ToolDeps`/`ToolResult`, `call-tool.ts`'s `TypedTool`, `provenance.ts`'s `markDefinition`/`isDefinitionOf`, `git/helpers.ts`'s failure helpers, `git/stash.ts`'s `gitStashTool`, and the test fixtures `_repo.ts`/`_standin.ts`/`_proc.ts`) and found every signature used matches what is actually exported. Confirmed the gh family files are byte-identical between the parent and this commit (acceptance check 6). All six Plan acceptance checks for s8/t1 map 1:1 onto the six test cases and each is genuinely exercised; the LLD's `buildGitFamilyTool`/`extendGitTool` signatures, postconditions and error conditions match the implementation exactly. The `executeTool` flow (schema check → approval → execute) confirms the LLD's ordering guarantee ("field the op does not take" / "pattern" refused before any approval request) holds for every path the tests actually exercise, and the field-pattern case specifically is enforced at the JSON-schema layer (pre-approval) per the gh module's own documented contract that op-table.ts imports unchanged. No HIGH/MED defects found in the reviewed code or its tests.

findings.message: The function-valued `cls` branch of `classOf` (used by `buildGitFamilyTool`'s own `approval`) is never exercised by any op built with `buildGitFamilyTool` in op-table.test.ts — all three fixture ops (read/wipe/feed) use a static `cls`. The only function-approval case tested (`extendGitTool keeps existing inputs and classes...`) exercises the *base* tool's (`gitStashTool`) own approval function via pass-through, not `classOf` itself.
findings.rationale: GitOpSpec explicitly types `cls` as `ApprovalClass | ((input: ToolInput) => ApprovalClass)` and the LLD's data-model notes a class that depends on input is a function and must be tested for both branches (for the real ops that will use this, in later tasks) — within t1 itself this engine branch has no direct unit case. I verified by reading that the one-line ternary is correct, so this is a coverage gap, not a demonstrated defect.

findings.message: The `spawnError` (missing-tool) and `timedOut` (+ the mutating-only unknown-outcome suffix) paths of `runIn` have no direct test in op-table.test.ts; none of the six tests simulate a missing git binary or a timeout.
findings.rationale: The LLD's postcondition for `buildGitFamilyTool` explicitly states "a command that did not start is missing-tool, one that was killed is timed-out and carries the unknown-outcome text when the op changes something," but none of the Plan's six acceptance checks for t1 require this scenario and none of the six tests cover it. I traced the logic by hand (the `fail` closure's conditional `original`/`message` parameters into `withFailure`) and it is correct, but it is unexercised at this layer.

tasks.summary: t2 adds git_inspect, a class-none, 27-op read-only family tool built on the s8 op-table builder (buildGitFamilyTool). Every op in GIT_INSPECT_OPS (describe, name-rev, cherry, shortlog, show-branch, grep, last-modified, count-objects, var, version, check-attr, check-ignore, check-mailmap, check-ref-format, get-tar-commit-id, diff-files, diff-index, diff-pairs, range-diff, show-index, verify-commit, verify-tag, verify-pack, fsck, fsck-objects, pack-redundant, repo) has a matching coverage.ts row owned 'covered' with toolIds ['git_inspect'] and a case, a matching test case in git-coverage.test.ts's RUN table, and a matching row in docs/daemon.md's generated table. A no-match exit (grep, check-ignore, check-ref-format, get-tar-commit-id, verify-commit, verify-tag) is handled via okCodes:[0,1] and parse functions that read run.code, giving found/valid/verified:false rather than a tool failure — confirmed both by git-inspect.test.ts's explicit no-match case and by the read() helper hard-coding cls:'none' for every op (never overridden), so gitInspectTool.approval always returns 'none', verified by git-inspect.test.ts's loop over every op. findings.message: merge-file current/base/other use path() but are listed in refs, so a leading-dash value passes schema validation and reaches the approval prompt before assertSafeArg rejects it at execute time.
findings.rationale: refs fields are supposed to use the dash-disallowing rev() pattern since they are positional args with no terminator; path() permits a leading dash.

findings.rationale: sibling fields bad and rev in the same op correctly use rev(); good is the one refs field left unpatterned.
